headline: 63 foreigners detained in Chittagong for running casino
summary: Police raided an eight-story building in West Jalalabad, seizing laptops and foreign currency from citizens of Laos, China, Pakistan, and Vietnam.
details: Police detained 63 foreign nationals from a single eight-story building in the West Jalalabad area of Khulshi police station, Chittagong, on allegations of operating an illegal gambling casino.
The raid, conducted on Thursday night based on secret intelligence, involved questioning foreign nationals residing on various floors of the building.
Authorities recovered over 50 laptops, various foreign currencies, and other equipment used for casino operations during the search.
The detainees, including citizens of Laos, Laos, China, Pakistan, and Vietnam, were transported from the building in prison vans on Friday morning.
Local residents reported that foreign nationals had been frequently visiting the building for approximately one month.

headline: Gold prices drop by 2,158 taka per bhori in Bangladesh
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has adjusted prices following a decline in the global market, bringing 22-carat gold down to 231,880 taka per bhori.
details: Gold prices in Bangladesh have decreased by a maximum of 2,158 taka per bhori over the last two days. The new rates became effective from 10 AM on Friday.

The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) stated that the price adjustment was made due to a drop in the prices of fine gold in the local market, primarily driven by a decline in the global gold market.
For 22-carat gold, the price has dropped to 231,880 taka per bhori. Meanwhile, 21-carat gold is now 221,441 taka, and 18-carat gold stands at 190,123 taka per bhori.
Traditional gold prices have also decreased by 1,516 taka, bringing the cost to 155,306 taka per bhori. All mentioned prices include VAT.
Silver prices have also seen a decline of 116 taka per bhori, with 22-carat silver now priced at 5,016 taka per bhori.
This follows a period of significant volatility. On January 29 of this year, gold prices hit a historic high of 286,000 taka per bhori after a sudden surge of 16,213 taka in a single day.
